note: MV2-3.5 deterministic factual research backstop. World Cup All-Star Team / Team-of-the-Tournament selections — a contemporaneous, position-aware tournament best-XI recognition that credits exactly the elite defenders and goalkeepers the recognition-weighted source set structurally under-credits (they win far fewer individual player-of-the-year awards than forwards). Scope is a BOUNDED gap-fill, not an exhaustive parse of every All-Star Team: it covers only the consensus-great defenders/keepers the MV2-9 recon-divergence read identified as under-credited by OUR model (etl/output/merit/RECON_DIVERGENCE.md). Each row is a citation-backed public fact transcribed from the named player's own public encyclopedia page — the player's display name as the canonical card carries it, their nation, the World Cup year of the selection, the source-stated position (DF/GK), a human detail, and a fetchable citation URL plus the specific claim it supports. The official Technical Study Group All-Star Team award ran 1994-2006; earlier (1930-1990) and later (2010+ 'Dream Team') editions are the widely-recorded tournament best-XI selections as documented on the cited pages — all carry the SAME modest bronze-tier strength in the EXISTING wc_legacy scorer (a best-XI-of-tournament selection, never an MVP). Only full-XI selections are sourced: 'Reserve', 'Fantasy Team' and 'Fans' All-Star Team' designations are deliberately excluded. NO rating numbers, rankings, OVR/channel/boost/override, NO recon values — only the selection record. The conservative linker treats these rows identically to parser rows (unique high-confidence link only; ambiguous withheld to review); an uncited row fails the build.
